template_params.tv_categories: TVs up to 43 inch, TVs 50-55 inch, TVs 65 inch and up

prompt: Joost, the pricing lead, is deciding whether to offer a TV and soundbar bundle price in next year's TV promotions, and asks whether orders with a TV on promotion held a soundbar more often in 2025. Take the orders with an order_ts from 2025-01-01 00:00:00 up to but not including 2026-01-01 00:00:00; order_ts holds UTC time. A TV order is one of those orders with at least one line for a product in one of the three TV categories: TVs up to 43 inch, TVs 50-55 inch and TVs 65 inch and up. A TV order is promoted when at least one of its TV lines carried a promotion (its promo_id is not missing), and regular otherwise; a promotion on any other line of the order does not count. A TV order has a soundbar when any line of the same order is for a product in the Soundbars category. Return one row for each kind of TV order, promoted and regular; a kind with no TV orders has no row. Return five columns, in this order: tv_offer, the text 'promoted' or 'regular'; n_tv_orders, the number of TV orders of that kind; n_with_soundbar, how many of them have a soundbar; attach_rate_pct, 100 times n_with_soundbar divided by n_tv_orders, rounded to 2 decimals; and attach_index, 100 times the kind's unrounded attach rate divided by the attach rate of all those TV orders together, rounded to 1 decimal. Count each order once, however many TV or soundbar lines it holds. Sort by tv_offer, alphabetically.
hints: Next, build a step with one row per 2025 TV order and its promotion status, before you look for soundbars.
For each TV order, ask whether a soundbar line exists in that same order; the index divides each kind's rate by the rate over every row of that step.
why_this_works: Each TV order becomes one row with its promotion status first, so EXISTS tests it for a soundbar without counting an order once per line.
